holidays.name: World Snake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate and appreciate snakes, those legless and misunderstood reptiles. Fans of all ages are encouraged to learn about snake species, visit reptile exhibits, and ditch the fear of slithery neighbors.
holidays.origin: Observed unofficially by reptile enthusiasts, herpetologists, and conservation groups around the world as a way to counter the bad reputation of snakes and promote their role in healthy ecosystems.
holidays.funFact: Snakes can't chew, so they swallow prey whole, and some species can unhinge their jaws, or more accurately stretch the ligaments connecting them, to eat animals much larger than their heads.

holidays.name: National Corn Fritters Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the golden, crispy, deep-fried delight of corn fritters. Whether served as a snack, side dish, or with a drizzle of syrup or honey, it is a day to fry up some batter and kernels.
holidays.origin: Like many American food days, it was established by food enthusiasts and promoted through food calendars as an excuse to enjoy a classic comfort food with deep roots in Southern and colonial American cooking.
holidays.funFact: Corn fritters were a staple of early American colonial kitchens, where cooks stretched cornmeal and kernels into a filling meal that could be fried in lard on a hearth.

holidays.name: National Fresh Spinach Day
holidays.description: A leafy green celebration of spinach, the vegetable made famous by a certain muscle-bound sailor. People are encouraged to toss it into salads, smoothies, and omelets.
holidays.origin: A food-calendar observance created to encourage people to eat more leafy greens, and often tied to the cultural legacy of Popeye the Sailor Man, who boosted US spinach consumption in the 1930s.
holidays.funFact: The popular myth that spinach is exceptionally high in iron is often blamed on a misplaced decimal point, though this story is itself debated by historians.

holidays.name: Guinea Pig Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A squeaky day to honor the wheeking, popcorning, hay-munching guinea pigs that share our homes. Owners treat their cavies to fresh veggies and extra floor time.
holidays.origin: Started by pet lovers and small animal communities online as a way to celebrate and raise awareness about the care and welfare of these social rodents.
holidays.funFact: Guinea pigs can't produce their own vitamin C, just like humans, so they need it from their diet. In Switzerland it is illegal to own just one because they get lonely.

holidays.name: World Emoji Day Weekend Vibes: Fresh Spinach and Fritter Fest
holidays.description: Not an official holiday but a fun unofficial one: pair a plate of corn fritters with spinach and toast to snakes and guinea pigs. A quirky mashup menu for July 16 celebrations.
holidays.origin: An invented mashup of the day's food observances, created for fun by quirky holiday fans who like to combine celebrations into one themed party.
holidays.funFact: Mashup holiday parties are popular on social media, where people create themed menus and activities that combine several observances falling on the same date.
